spans.s:
√1naś (náśyati; nanā́śa, neśús; ánaśat;
naṅkṣyáti [936]; naṣṭá; nāśáyati). be
missing; get lost; vanish; perish, be
ruined. [cf. νεκ-ρός, ‘dead’; Lat. nex,
‘death’; nocēre, ‘harm.’]
+ vi, get lost; perish; caus. cause to disappear;
 bring to nought, 81^20.

√2naś (náśati, -te; nanā́śa; ā́naṭ [833]).
attain; reach, come up to, 74^1; w. acchā,
draw hither, 76^11. [see √1aś, ‘reach’: cf.
Lat. nac-tus sum, ‘am having reached’;
AS. neāh, comp. neār, superl. neāhst, Eng.
nigh, near (as comp., Macbeth ii. 3. 146),
next; AS. ge-neah, ‘it reaches, es reicht, it
suffices’; ge-nōh, Eng. e-nough.]
+ pra, reach to, hit; fall upon, 78^8.

nas [491], encl. pron. form of 1st pers. [cf.
νώ, ‘we two’; Lat. nōs, ‘us.’]
[]
nasa, for nás in cpds [1315c].

nā́sā, dual f. the two nostrils, the nose.
[transfer-form (399) fr. nás, strong nā́s.]

nā́sikā, f. nostril; dual, the two nostrils;
the nose. [nā́sā, 1222c 1.]

nāstika, a. subst. atheist, infidel, not believing
the Vedas and Purānas. [fr.
na + asti, ‘there is not,’ 1314b.]
